## Conference overview

*Preview by Jonathan Von Tobel, p. 283. Reproduced in full.*


> The time at the top of the country has seemingly come to an end for the SEC.

> It has been three years since a member of the conference won a national championship.

> The Big Ten has dominated the last three seasons, all with different champions.

> The conversation all offseason has been about the SEC reclaiming its throne, and there is certainly a strong chance the conference can do just that with its depth of championship contenders.

> Georgia — the last SEC team to win it all — looks primed to grab its third title of the Kirby Smart era.

> The Bulldogs have a Heisman Trophy contender in quarterback Gunner Stockton and one of the most experienced rosters in the country.

> Texas has the experience as well, and the blue-chip prospect at quarterback in Arch Manning.

> Steve Sarkisian has some CFP wins under his belt and is dying to add to that this season.

> Given the additions the Longhorns made in the portal, as well as the returning production throughout the roster, the market believes this team is a true contender.

> Then, you get to some of the dark-horse contenders for both a conference title and national championship.

> Alabama and Texas A&M both made the CFP last season, but shared similar fates in being dispatched by the eventual participants in the national championship game.

> The Crimson Tide will have to work in a new quarterback, but they do have a talented roster with a great defense.

> The difference between the two is the experience Marcel Reed has at quarterback.

> Let’s not forget Ole Miss, which finished a drive short of a berth in the final, or Oklahoma, which returns most of the best defense in the country.

> The expectations for the SEC are always a national championship.

> This year is no different, and the conference boasts many potential contenders.

> The depth of the conference in terms of quality is not on par with the Big Ten, but no one will be shocked if a program from this conference is hoisting a trophy come January. sec

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 283):**

> It has been three years since a member of the conference won a national championship.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 283*

> Alabama and Texas A&M both made the CFP last season, but shared similar fates in being dispatched by the eventual participants in the national championship game.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 283*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 16 of 16 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Alabama Crimson Tide** (p. 284) — After missing out on the College Football Playoff in his first season at the helm, Kalen DeBoer led Alabama to the CFP in 2025.

- **Arkansas Razorbacks** (p. 286) — Arkansas has won nine games just once since its last doubledigit win season, which was in 2011.

- **Auburn Tigers** (p. 288) — The last winning season came in 2019, in Gus Malzahn’s penultimate season as head coach.

- **Florida Gators** (p. 290) — They have just one bowl win since the Orange Bowl victory over Virginia in 2019, and the program has not appeared in the CFP rankings since 2020.

- **Georgia Bulldogs** (p. 292) — Since 2017, Georgia has participated in every SEC Championship Game but one, which took place in 2020.

- **Kentucky Wildcats** (p. 294) — However, his record had been getting consistently worse, bottoming out last season with a paltry two wins.

- **LSU Tigers** (p. 296) — Lane Kiffin had a LeBron James-esque winter in 2025 when dragged out the drama of leaving Ole Miss in the midst of a playoff chase in order to take the job at LSU.

- **Mississippi State Bulldogs** (p. 298) — Mississippi State got off to a promising 4-0 SU and ATS start to the season in 2025, but once the Bulldogs made it to SEC play, the wheels came off.
